label: paragraph_title
text: On Other Routes

label: text
text: The s.s. "Wing On" spick and span after overhaul, is alongside her wharf. She will be going to Kongmoon in a very few days and will be the pioneer there as the Sze Yan S.S. Co. have not; it is reported, renewed their charter to a syndicate, of the s.s. "Tai Lee" and "On Lee."

label: text
text: Then again there is the "Fook On" ready to leave in a day or two for Wuchow, on the West River. She will be the first bout back on that run.

label: paragraph_title
text: Samchun Puses?

label: text
text:
There are still a great many other river steambonds. Some of the smaller ones which changed over to Chinese registry during the strike are expected to remain on up-river runs, but the majority are preparing to return as soon as conditions and finance permit.
Normal conditions prevail above and between Samchun, the border stations on the railway.

label: text
text: An unconfirmed report says that although the armed pickets are now in Canton, five unarmed pickets in multi-type staying near Samchun to collect travelling passes hitherto issued to passengers, when and as such return; but there is no interference.

label: text
text: The improved tone in local markets is slightly more pronounced. Merchants expect delay of a few days more before cargo begins to move freely.

label: text
text: Except from Swatow there is no unfavourable report about the piekets.

label: text
text: The Merchant-Labour examination shed on the Canton Fund is being demolished but a new mat- shed is springing up, in which the Nationalist Government will collect their temporary taxes.

label: text
text: The strikters have also asked Cannon merchants to clear from their examination shed cargo remaining therein.

label: text
text:
The General Chamber of Commerce in Canton has, on the other hand, circularised other chambers. It states that the Strike Committee has proposed the formation of an organisation of liquidate stocks of British cargo after which members will not deal in them any more.
Other than steps by agitators to promote popular boycott in Canton of British trade and British goods, there is as yet no evidence of the boycott being called, off in

label: paragraph_title
text: BRITISH SHIPPING.

label: paragraph_title
text: Feelers Put Out by Local Companies.

label: text
text: Now that the official declaration by Canton of the cessation of boycott activities has been made, the local British shipping companies are seeking to ascertain the position as regards trade by the only practical method—by sending up ships the result of which trips will largely determine future plans as regards sailing dates.

label: text
text: The China Navigation Company (Butterfield and Swire) s.s. "Sinkiang" left Hong Kong for Canton yesterday, this being an extension of the run from Shanghai to Hong Kong. Before the strike, this, together with other ships, was on the Shanghai-Hong Kong-Canton run.

label: text
text: First Since Strike.

label: text
text:
The "Sinkiang" is the first of these B. and S. ships, since the boycott trouble originated to make the trip to Canton. It berthed at the B. and S. wharf at Pak-hok-tung and will leave later for Hong Kong and Shanghai. No regular schedule has as yet been arranged, the sailing of the "Sinkiang" being in the nature of a test trip.
To the Indo-China S. N. Co. (Jar'dime's) vessels on the same run (the "Foishing" and "Cheongshing" have already made trips to Canton and left later for Shanghai) has been added the "Hopsang" which leaves for Canton at daybreak tomorrow.

label: paragraph_title
text: Steamboat Co.

label: text
text: The difficulty with regard to the running by the Steamboat Co. of night boats to Canton is the restriction with regard to night passage in the martial war area of Bocca Tigris forts. The Company is carrying out negotiations as a result of which it is hoped that the full morning and night service to and from Canton will be resumed next week.

text:

passengers and cargo.

label: text
text: The C. N. Co.'s "Fatshan" is coming down from Canton to-day —the first boat to leave since Oct. 10.

label: text

EUROPEAN INSULTED BY
TAXI DRIVER.

label: text
text: The dangerous practice of carrying protruding beams from motor lorries was referred to in the traffic summonses heard by Major C. Willson at the Central Magistracy this morning.

label: text
text: THE WEEKLY LIST.

label: text
text: Finés ranging up to $12 were imposed on the offenders among whom were a number of car drivers caught driving in a dangerous or negligent manner.

label: text
text: The offence of a driver in disregarding a signal to stop and scattering a squad of police near the Queen's Theatre was considered to be more serious than the others and this was met with a fine of $20.

label: text
text:
A taxicab driver, charged with using abusive language to his fare, Mr. T. F. O'Sullivan, denied the offence, but admitted that he failed to complete the journey.
Traffic Sergt. Hopkins said that the complainant was absent, as he thought the case would be heard next week.

label: text
text: A suggestion from the defendant that the passenger failed to understand him was turned down by Sub-Inspector Alexander and His Worship adjourned the summons for one week to hear evidence.

label: paragraph_title
text: PORT ACTIVITIES BEGIN SHORTLY.

label: paragraph_title
text: Y.M.C.A. NOTES:

label: text
text: FIRST LADIES' NIGHT.

label: text
text: The plans for the season are now almost complete and a programme will shortly be issued showing the varied activities of the Association.

label: text
text: The Sports Committee is at work arranging the following branches of sport: golf, water polo, hockey, bowls and football. It is intended to arrange matches with other clubs.

label: text
text: Outdoor games such as baseball, volley ball, basket ball, etc., with some physical training, will take place on the ground at the rear of the building and on the roof, Mondays and Tuesdays, from 6 to 7 in the evenings. Shower baths are at the disposal of members not residing in the building. These games will commence on Monday, October 18.

label: text
text: The tennis ground looks promising and will be used as soon as the necessary work is completed.

label: text
text:
Members are asked to notify the Secretary of their intentions to participate in any of the branches of sport mentioned.
The indoor activities, commence on Thursday, Oct. 28, with the Literary and Debating Club dinner, other events being Ping-pong cup championship (kiock out tournament), last date for entries being Oct. 24; draughts tournament and sing-songs.

label: text
text: The first, Ladies' Night will be held on Thursday, November 4.

label: paragraph_title
text: LOTTERY TICKETS.

label: text
text: SKIPPED HIS BAIL

label: text
text: A Chinese named Leung Min, alleged to be an extensive dealer in illegal lottery ventures, failed to appear at the Central Magistracy this morning to answer a charge of possession of 683 Macao lottery tickets of a face value of $7,956.

label: text
text: Defendant was arrested with the tickets at Upper Lascar Row yesterday by a Chinese detective and was released on bail of $250.

label: text
text: It was stated that defendant had been arrested along with three others one year ago for a similar offence, but on that occasion also he failed to attend court while out of bail.

label: text
text: The Magistrate ordered the bail money to be estreated.

label: paragraph_title
text: WUCHANG LATEST.

label: text
text:
How Treachery Sold Besieged
Generals

label: text
text: Wuchang is now in the hands of the southerners' Army. Many disarmed northern troops landed at Hankow today (Monday).—Naval Despatch.

label: text
text: Wuchang finally passed into southern hands this afternoon apparently as the result of treachery on the part of a certain section of its defenders, who, opening the gate, admitted the besiegers.

label: text
text: General Liu Yu-chun was taken prisoner in the Boone College compound and is arriving at Hankow under escort this evening, while it is reported that General Chen Chia-mo has also been captured.—Reuter.

label: text
text: [Note]: These two Wu Pei-fu generals commanded the besieged garrison.]

label: paragraph_title
text: REPORTS BY MAIL.

label: text
text: Southerners Pressing Hard on

label: text
text: The following 'war reports, to hand' by mail, confirm the despatches published in the "China Mail" last week, prior to the southerners' embarking on their coup.

label: text
text: Reports from Kiukiang received in Shanghai to-day state that severe fighting is taking place within a short distance of the city with the southerner pressing hard. In consequence of this Marshal Sun Chuan-fang has sent an urgent call to Wusueh for the immediate despatch of 7,000 troops to relieve the situation.

label: text
text: The general war situation remains virtually unchanged with fighting still in progress on the Nanchang front. — “Shanghai Mercury.”

label: paragraph_title
text: Recapture of Te-an:

label: text
text: A telegram from Kuikang dated Oct. 6, says:—The 8th Mixed-Brigade under the command of General Yen Ching-tsung made an onslaught on the southern troops stationed at Te-an, from the direction of the south of the town, from dawn of October 5 until noon, and finally re-captured Te-an.

label: text
text: The southerners are reported to have retreated to a hilly district south of Te-an. The Allied troops, some 10,000 men strong, concentrated at the rear of Te-an, left there for Te-an on October 5 under command of General Chou Hung-chi.

label: text
text: In the region south-west of Nanchang, the 2nd and the 3rd Allied army have been gradually pressing hard the main body of General Chang Kai-shek's troops since October 4.—“Toho.”

label: text
text:
Casualties of Both Sides.
Xinjiang: Oct. 7

label: text
text: The number of casualties of the Allied forces is estimated at 4,000 men, while that of the southern troops are more than 5,000.

label: text
text: Soldiers are fatigued with fighting, and the sentiment in favour of peace has become more pronounced than ever. Marshal Sun Chuan-fang is expected to inspect the battlefields and to encourage his troops.—“Toho.”

label: text
text: Many trainloads of Chang Tsung-chang's troops have passed down the Peking-Hankow Railway toward Paotingfu. The two Russian-named armoured trains called "Shantung" and "Honan" have left Peking for the same route. General Chu Yu-pu is at Paotingfu with other Fengtien generals, who are apparently more concerned with keeping Wu Pei-fu under control than with suppressing the Cantonese.

label: paragraph_title
text: COPPER PRICE

label: paragraph_title
text: AMERICAN PRODUCERS COMBINE.

label: text
text: RITISH INTERESTS INVOLVEI

label: text
text: The Government has approved of the American copper producers co-operating for the establishment of the price of domestic copper in the foreign markets. All the leading producers, representing an enormous aggregate capital are incorporated in the new Company. "The Copper Exporters" under the presidency of Mr. Kelly, President of the Anaconda Copper Company. An effort will be made to sell direct to consumers except where conditions make it desirable to sell to distributors.

label: text
text: The foreign associate members of the combine include the British Metals Corporations, the Rio Tinto Company, and the lending South American, German, French, and Belgian interests. — Reuter's American Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: ASHORE.

label: paragraph_title
text: STRANGE DISCOVERY ON AN ISLAND.

label: text
text: 33 PEOPLE ALIVE.

label: text
text: A strange tale of the sea has been revealed in a report made at Stanley Police Station "by Chan Tong, master of the Cheung Hok grocery shop at Po To Au Island, which is near Clear Water Bay and on the other side of Junk Bay.

label: text
text: At 9 o'clock on Saturday morning a report was made at the shop by boat people that a number of people had been washed ashore alive at the back of the island.

label: text
text: Shop employees were sent out to investigate and found the story to be true, as they found 30 men and three women on the beach, apparently the survivors of a junk which had foundered in the equally weather during the weekend.

label: text
text: Some of the survivors appeared to be in a bad way with the hardships they had undergone in swimming ashore. The master of the shop took them all in and provided them with food and clothing.

label: text
text: The people spoke the Hoklo dialect, and the police are without any further report from them to account for their being cast on the island.

label: text
text: A Chinese was fined $250, or three months' hard labour, by Mr. E. W. Hamilton at the Central Magistracy this morning for having several tons of coal aboard a junk at Shaukiwan in regard to which he was unable to give a satisfactory explanation.

label: paragraph_title
text: STRIKES OBSOLETE.

label: paragraph_title
text:
REMARKABLE ADDRESS BY
LABOURITE

label: text
text: EXTREMISTS' OUTBURSTS

label: text
text: Rugby, Oct. 11.

label: text
text:
Lively scenes marked the opening of the annual conference of the Labour Party at Margate.
Mr. Robert Williams, in delivering the presidential address, dealt with the mining crisis. He declared that preparations for this industrial struggle had not been confined to the coal owners and those supporting them. Individuals in the Labour Party's own ranks had constantly talked of preparing for it. The Labour Party's own ranks had constantly talked of preparing for it. The Labour Party was the foremost party in condemning militarism in international affairs. If peace was to be sought internationally by methods of conciliation, let industrial peace be sought by the same methods. They must preserve the right of Unions to strike, but conciliation played an important part in their work.

label: text
text: Men would be heard saying: "Get ready for the next general strike." He would reply that they should read the unfavourable agreements upon which the railwaymen and transport workers resumed work after the general strike last May. He had had over twelve years' experience of strikes, and he knew that it was not easy to secure a return to work on terms as satisfactory as those obtaining before action was taken.

label: text
text: In regard to the miners, Mr. Williams declared:

label: text
text: "Their decision to continue the dispute is heroic. They may be likened to a sightless Samson feeling for the grip of the pillars of the temple, the crashing of which may engulf this thing which we call British civilisation."

label: text
text: The Miners' Conference, he said, asked for an embargo on foreign coal. An embargo had been ineffective during the cbal stoppage of 1921. What hope was there of success in 1926? It was a despairing policy.

label: text
text: He concluded: "The Communist Party and minority movement still believe in a general strike. The Labour Party looks with confidence to the General Election."

label: paragraph_title
text: Sentiment Applauded.

label: text
text: Mr. Williams's outspoken remarks were greeted with violent outbursts from the extremists present. He was charged with making insolent attacks on the miners. At times he continued only with difficulty, but his final remark—to the effect that the Labour Party stood for constitutional action—was loudly applauded by the great majority of the delegates present at the conference.—British Wireless Service.
